messages:
customer-acme: Hey team — we're seeing streaming responses cut off mid-output then the client reconnects and gets a duplicate billing event for the same user/interaction. Happens ~30-60s into long responses. No obvious 5xx in our app logs.

ruth-support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a minimal repro? request headers, `Last-Event-ID` behavior, and whether you rotate auth tokens on the client? :eyes:

customer-acme: Repro steps below. We rotate tokens every 25s (short-lived token for security), and the client will reconnect with a fresh token. When reconnect happens the stream resumes but the charge shows twice in our billing UI. Also noticed the client sometimes receives the final chunk only after reconnect (partial output first, then remainder).

customer-acme: Repro (curl):
```
# open stream
curl -N \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <rotating-token-1>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/outputs?model=redwood-xl"\
```
Then after ~25s rotate to token-2 and the client reconnects:
```
curl -N \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <rotating-token-2>" \
  -H "Last-Event-ID: <last_event_id_seen>" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/outputs?model=redwood-xl"\
```
Observed behavior: first session shows partial streaming text and then closes; second session resumes but our billing shows two invoice lines for same conversation id.

matt-eng: Thanks. Two likely vectors: (1) token rotation leads to new session id on server -> server treats as new request and charges again, (2) proxies or intermediate TCP timeouts drop the SSE connection and the server doesn't flush/mark as completed so client reconnects and server replays final tokens.

ida-obs: I pulled traces for the last failed run (trace id: trace-0ab9). Server logs show: `WARN stream-session: connection lost, upstream read timeout after 28.3s, session_id=svc-84f, last_event_id=evt-732`. Then 1s later we see a fresh session: `INFO stream-session: session resumed from last_event_id=evt-732, new_session_id=svc-9ac, auth_subject=acct-775`. That's exactly the timeline the customer described.

kevin-sre: Are we using comment pings on these streams? Some HTTP proxies drop idle SSE streams if no bytes flow; comment pings (lines starting with `:`) keep the connection alive at the HTTP level. If the client is sending no activity for long sequences the TCP keepalive alone may not prevent idle HTTP intermediate termination.

ruth-support: customer says they don't see comment pings in the bytes. They rely on token activity only.

matt-eng: Actionable suggestions:
1) Short-term: recommend client enable comment pings from server every 15s (or have client send a lightweight `:ping\n\n` SSE comment) to keep proxies happy.
2) Medium-term: support a resume token header (e.g., `X-Resume-Token`) so reconnects with rotated auth can be verified as the same logical session and not double-billed.
3) Billing: add server-side idempotency/dedupe for resume windows — if `last_event_id` within a grace window and same conversation fingerprint, avoid creating a second charge.

ida-obs: Also logs show `401 auth failure` in a couple of reconnect attempts when token rotated during reconnect handshake. That yields a short closed socket and client retries, producing multiple session creations in a short window.

customer-acme: Is there anything we can change client-side now? We can try to preserve a resume token across rotation and present it on reconnect. We do not want to extend token lifetime.

matt-eng: Good plan. For immediate repro and diagnostics, please run this sequence and attach full request/response bytes (use `--raw` or `--trace-ascii`). Outline:
- Start stream with token-A and record `last_event_id` values as they arrive.
- Wait for token rotation, attempt reconnect using token-B with header `Last-Event-ID: <id>` and add custom header `X-Client-Resume: <client-uuid>`
- Capture server logs and single-stream request ids.

kevin-sre: From infra side: I'll check proxy idle timeouts (ALB/nginx/Cloudflare) — default idle TCP timeouts often 60s/120s. If comment pings are missing, the proxy will terminate and we won't observe a graceful EOF. We should lower our upstream read timeout split logs to differentiate client vs proxy closes.

deploy-bot: deploy started: enable-stream-heartbeat-v0.1 -> staging (d: kevin-sre)

ida-obs: One more thing: our streaming runtime has a boolean `charge_on_new_session` flag that flips when last_event_id is missing. If reconnect includes `Last-Event-ID` we should prefer resume-path and not bill again. Looks like the flag was false for this model until a recent config change; I'm going to flip it for the affected model in staging.

ruth-support: Customer — is it OK if we flip `charge_on_new_session` for your tenant in staging for a smoke test? We can coordinate a quick window.

customer-acme: Yes please. We'll test in 30m. We can also instrument client to pass `X-Client-Resume`.

matt-eng: Suggested server-side quick mitigations (in order):
- Accept `Last-Event-ID` + `X-Client-Resume` as proof-of-resume and avoid duplicative charge if event IDs overlap within 2 minutes.
- Emit a server comment ping `:heartbeat\n\n` every 12s for active streams. This buys time against proxies.
- When auth rotates during reconnect, return `409 Conflict` with `Retry-After` and `Resume-Allowed: true` instead of spinning up a new session. Client can then reattempt resume without causing a new charge.

kevin-sre: I'll open infra ticket to audit ALB/nginx idle timeouts + ensure streaming TCP keepalive and proxy buffering are disabled for these endpoints.

ida-obs: I'll patch runtime to log `billing_marker` on resume paths so we can query for duplicates and retroactively credit customers if needed.

ruth-support: Thanks all. Customer — after you test, please paste the staging trace id here. We'll keep this thread open and escalate to billing if duplicates are observed after we've flipped the flag. :pray:

customer-acme: Tested — staging flip looks promising. Stream stayed alive longer and no duplicate invoice lines in the small batch we ran. Staging trace id: trace-0ac2. We'll run production canary after your infra change.

matt-eng: Great. Follow-ups:
- kevin-sre to update proxy timeouts and confirm by EOD (assignee: kevin-sre)
- ida-obs to deploy `charge_on_new_session=false` for model redwood-xl in prod-staging and add `billing_marker` logs (assignee: ida-obs)
- engineering to draft `X-Resume-Token` spec and `409` resume-friendly response semantics (assignee: matt-eng)

kevin-sre: Confirmed: ALB idle timeout was 60s, raising to 180s and enabling `proxy_set_header Connection "keep-alive"` on nginx pools. Will monitor for reconnects.

ruth-support: Closing loop with customer later today after prod canary. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
